annotations.title: Buscar empresas que usam um ERP

description: Finds companies that run one of the ERPs asked (totvs, sap_business_one, sap, omie, sankhya, senior, linx, netsuite, dynamics, bling, tiny, contaazul, egestor, vhsys, marketup, gestaoclick, nomus), each proved with public evidence: a job post the company itself published, its site or its domain's e-mail setup. The same search, company check and filters as the "Usa ERP" signal (recruiters, accounting offices, ERP vendors and consultancies, and posts published for another company are left out), as a one-off list instead of a daily feed. Candidates come from job posts that name the ERP: Nock's job index first (LinkedIn, its largest source, read every 6 hours for posts naming the ERPs and their modules, plus Gupy, Vagas.com, Indeed, Glassdoor, Sólides and others), and when it has fewer than asked LinkedIn is searched live in the same call; then openings in an area that runs it (hiringArea: fiscal_contabil by default, fiscal, contabil, controladoria, financeiro, compras), then companies of the market (location, industry, companySizes). Filters on the job post that brought the company, read BEFORE any check (a candidate that fails them is never checked nor charged): postedWithinDays (1 to 180, only posts published within that many days; a company with no dated post is left out) and jobPostTitles (words or titles, e.g. ["analista", "coordenador", "controller"], accents and case aside; a title of several words needs each). A company is delivered only as the post's employer: never a recruiter, a hidden employer ("Confidencial") or an accounting office, never a site of another company with a similar name (checked against the Registry's CNPJ and state), and, with companySizes, never one whose headcount (the job index's or the Registry's estimate) is outside them. It also looks up one decision maker at each company (jobTitle, default "CFO, Diretor Financeiro, Controller"; area "financeiro" is an option that keeps only finance decision makers and leaves out other areas' titles such as "Controller Jurídico", without it anyone matching jobTitle; findPeople false skips it; withEmail adds the work e-mail) and saves every company in a sheet before it returns: the ERP, the evidence excerpt and its address on the company, the decision maker as a person row of that company. sheetId adds to an existing sheet and skips the companies it already has; without it a sheet named sheetName (default "Usa <ERPs>") is reused or created. limit 10 by default, 25 at most. Two steps: without confirmed it runs nothing, charges nothing and returns maxCredits, the most the call can cost, and candidates (how many companies of Nock's job index pass the filters before any check); with confirmed true it runs and charges. Prices, only for the companies delivered (the companies checked and left out are never charged): 4 per company delivered, plus its own check: 1 credit when a check ran now for it and 6 when a job post was read for it (an answer kept from an earlier check, or a post of Nock's own job index, is free); 8 per decision maker found by search (a partner the Receita names is free); 3 per work e-mail found. Finishes within about 85 seconds and returns the companies (name, domain, cnpj, city and uf from the Registry, empty when not found; ERP, confidence, evidence source, url, excerpt and postedAt; jobPost with its title, url and postedAt; decision maker with LinkedIn), counts, creditsCharged, leftOutBeforeCharge, sheetId and sheetPath. partial true means the time ran out or a source failed before the limit was reached; "more" says how to continue (the same input with the returned sheetId brings the next companies, and the ones already in the sheet are neither checked nor charged again).

area.description: Optional: only decision makers of this area. "financeiro" keeps finance people (CFO, finance director or manager, a finance controller) and leaves out other areas' titles such as "Controller Jurídico"; without jobTitle it also looks for the finance titles. Left out: anyone matching jobTitle, as before.

confirmed.description: false or absent: returns the most it can cost and runs nothing. true: runs and charges.

erps.description: Any of these ERPs (totvs, sap_business_one, sap, omie, sankhya, senior, linx, netsuite, dynamics, bling, tiny, contaazul, egestor, vhsys, marketup, gestaoclick, nomus); sap_business_one needs evidence naming Business One, sap is any SAP.

findPeople.description: false brings only the companies, no decision maker. Default true.

hiringArea.description: The openings that bring the candidates: fiscal_contabil (default), fiscal, contabil, controladoria, financeiro or compras.

industry.description: The sector in plain words, e.g. "indústria de alimentos".

jobPostTitles.description: Optional: only companies whose job post's title has one of these words or titles, accents and case aside, e.g. ["analista", "coordenador", "controller"] (a title of several words needs each of them). Applied before any check: a post of another title is never checked nor charged. hiringArea still picks which openings are searched.

jobTitle.description: Who to find at each company, titles tried in order, comma-separated. Default "CFO, Diretor Financeiro, Controller".

limit.description: Companies to bring, 10 by default, 25 at most.

location.description: A state or city, e.g. "SP" or "Curitiba, PR". Brazil when left out.

postedWithinDays.description: Optional, 1 to 180: only companies whose job post was published within this many days ("abriram vaga nos últimos 30 dias" is 30). Applied before any check: an older post, or a company with no dated post, is never checked nor charged. Each company returns its post's date (jobPost.postedAt).

sheetId.description: An existing sheet to add the companies to; companies already in it are skipped. Without it, a new sheet is made.

sheetName.description: The name of the sheet to use or make when there is no sheetId (a sheet of that name is reused).

withEmail.description: Also look up each decision maker's work e-mail. Default false.
